item.title: Mastra AI releases skills framework for building AI applications with TypeScript
item.description:
Mastra AI releases skills framework for building AI applications with TypeScript

Mastra is a framework for building AI-powered applications and agents with a modern TypeScript stack. It supports skill discovery via the .well-known standard and provides installation methods through npx skills add https://mastra.ai/.

🔍 Overview

Mastra introduces a skills framework for developing AI applications using TypeScript. The system enables automatic skill discovery through the .well-known skills standard, allowing developers to discover capabilities without manual configuration.

🧩 How it works

The framework implements progressive disclosure with reference files covering multiple development aspects:

Reference File Purpose
create-mastra.md Setup & Installation
embedded-docs.md Find APIs in node_modules/@mastra/*/dist/docs/
remote-docs.md Fetch from https://mastra.ai/llms.txt
common-errors.md Common errors and solutions
migration-guide.md Version upgrade workflows
mastra-api.md Inspect and call resources on local, platform, or remote servers
platform.md Build and deploy apps to Mastra Platform
gateway.md One key for many providers, failover, spend tracking
trace-query.md Select completed traces with recursive predicates
feedback.md Report verified bugs and concrete documentation defects

The main skill file teaches core concepts and routes to appropriate reference files based on user questions. A standalone Factory skill enables coding agents using mastra api factory, covering first-use CLI/login checks and URL-based connection capabilities.

⚙️ Key details

Installation Methods

  • npx skills add mastra-ai/skills
  • gh skill install mastra-ai/skills
  • git clone https://github.com/mastra-ai/skills.git (then configure agent to load from cloned directory)

Well-Known Discovery

  • RFC 8615 Well-Known URI: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/
  • Index: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/index.json
  • Mastra skill: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/mastra/SKILL.md
  • Factory skill: https://mastra.ai/.well-known/skills/mastra-factory/SKILL.md

Factory Skill Features

The Factory skill is a comprehensive skill for AI development that covers:

  • First-use CLI/login checks
  • URL-based connection from any directory
  • Project and queue summaries
  • Work-item session/thread and memory inspection
  • Health interpretation
  • User-authorized operations

Installation Options

  • npx skills add mastra-ai/skills --skill mastra-factory (install just the Factory skill with interactive agent/scope selection)
  • Global install with --agent <agent> -g for supported agents explicitly
  • Multi-agent installs can partially succeed; verify with npx skills list (add -g for global scope)

🚀 Availability

The skills repository is available via:

  • GitHub: git clone https://github.com/mastra-ai/skills.git
  • RFC 8615 Well-Known URI for automatic discovery
  • Direct URL installation: npx skills add https://mastra.ai/

The repository is served via Apache-2.0 license and welcomes contributions through forking, improvement to SKILL.md files, testing with development workflows, and submitting pull requests.

item.title: Businesses Rehire Staff After AI Fails to Replace Human Skills
item.description:
Businesses Rehire Staff After AI Fails to Replace Human Skills

A growing number of companies are reversing AI-driven redundancies after discovering that human skills remain irreplaceable in key areas.

🔍 Overview

Business leaders are backtracking on job cuts attributed to AI, with many rehiring staff after realizing the technology could not fully replicate human capabilities.

⚙️ Key details

  • 39% of business leaders made employees redundant because of AI.
  • Of those, 55% admit they made the wrong decisions about those redundancies.

🏢 Company examples

Company Action Reason
Ford Rehired over 300 engineers AI failed to match their skills and experience
Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) Reversed 45 job cuts Described the cuts as an “error”
IBM Rehired staff after AI handled routine HR requests AI struggled with complex judgment, empathy, and ethical reasoning

📊 Industry outlook

Research from Gartner estimates that by 2027, 50% of companies that attributed headcount reductions to AI will rehire staff to perform similar functions under different job titles.

💡 Why it matters

Unique human skills like critical thinking, creativity, and ethical reasoning cannot yet be replicated by AI.

#AI #jobcuts #rehiring #workforce #automation #skills

Source: AI layoffs reverse giving young workers a new opportunity

item.title: New AI agent skills for real engineering workflows
item.description:
New AI agent skills for real engineering workflows

A new set of AI agent skills has been introduced to address common failure modes in AI-assisted software development, focusing on alignment and process control.

🔍 Overview

The skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable, working with any model. They are based on decades of engineering experience and aim to fix misalignment between developers and agents, a frequent issue in AI-assisted development.

🧩 How it works

The skills are available in two formats:

  • Claude Code plugin: Installs as a managed, read-only bundle that updates automatically when new versions are shipped. Users subscribe rather than fork.
  • skills.sh: Copies editable skill files into the project, allowing users to modify and customize them.

Installation options include:

  • claude plugins install mattpocock-skills
  • /plugin install mattpocock-skills (from inside a session)
  • npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills

The installer lets users select which skills to adopt, with setup-matt-pocock-skills recommended as one of them. For the editable version, skills are written as ordinary files in the repository, and updates are pulled manually via npx skills update.

⚙️ Key details

The skills address two primary challenges:

  • Misalignment: A communication gap between users and agents, where the agent fails to understand requirements. The fix is a “grilling session” using:
    • /grill-me: For non-code use cases.
    • /grill-with-docs: Adds documentation to improve alignment.
  • Jargon: Agents often struggle with project-specific terminology. /grill-with-docs includes a shared language document to help agents decode jargon.

The installer also configures project-specific settings, such as:

  • Issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, or local files).
  • Labels for ticket triage (used by /triage).
  • Location for generated documentation.

🚀 Availability

  • The Claude Code plugin is available in the official marketplace, with automatic updates.
  • A native Codex plugin is planned (roadmap referenced in .agents/adr/0002-ship-as-a-claude-code-plugin.md).
  • Users can join a newsletter with ~60,000 other developers to stay updated on new skills and changes.

💡 Why it matters

The skills aim to improve AI-assisted development by:

  • Reducing misalignment between users and agents.
  • Providing composable, adaptable tools for real engineering workflows.
  • Offering flexibility in installation and customization.
